decisions.reason: Strip 3, line 1 of רבונו של עולם, 'אֲנִי ___'. The word clearly has a mark under the lamed and a mark inside the final kaf. At this resolution I can't tell whether the mark inside the kaf is a shva (B שֶׁלָּךְ) or a qamats (A שֶׁלְּךָ), or whether the lamed mark is qamats+dagesh or shva+dagesh. My weak visual lean is B, but I'm not confident enough, and I won't let my memory of the familiar wording decide it.

Same line, the second occurrence 'וַחֲלוֹמוֹתַי ___'. Same problem as id 0: the vowel inside the final kaf and under the lamed can't be resolved. I judged this occurrence on its own rather than assuming it matches id 0. Weak lean is again B.

Strips 3/4, end of line 2, 'שֶׁיִּהְיוּ כ_ל'. The kaf has a qamats, but I can't confirm from the strip whether there is a dagesh dot inside the kaf. Grammar alone (a vowel-final word before it) doesn't settle what was printed.

Strips 4/5 clearly read 'וְיִתְקַיְּמוּ בִי וּבָהֶם כַּחֲלוֹמוֹת יוֹסֵף הַצַּדִּיק'. The word is printed between בִי and כַּחֲלוֹמוֹת, so A really leaves out printed text. This is not a structural split.

Strip 5, line 3: 'עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה ___ וּכְמֵי'. The printed word has five letters, with a yod after the bet (ר־ב־י־נ־ו). I couldn't see A's meteg-only spelling without the yod. I can't make out whether there is a separate meteg, so the literal has none.
Strip 5, line 3: 'וּכְמֵי ___ עַל יְדֵי אֱלִישָׁע'. The word is visibly short, four letters with no yod after the resh. This is a defective spelling, not a typo.
Strips 7/8, line starting the response to יִשָּׂא: a maqaf is clearly printed between וּמְצָא and חֵן.
Strip 8: 'קִוִּינוּ הֱיֵה ___ לַבְּקָרִים'. The word is printed full, with a holam-vav (ז־ר־ו־ע־ם), not the defective זְרֹעָם.

Strip 8: אַף is the last word on the line, and a small raised stroke after the pe looks like a line-final maqaf. יְשׁוּעָתֵֽנוּ (with meteg) starts the next line. The line break is just layout, not a separation in the text.
